correctness.rationale: For each prime-exponent partition the exponent partition, the recursive-divisor value the recursive-divisor value of the signature is computed exactly from the defining proper-divisor recurrence. A rearrangement argument proves that the least odd integer of that signature is the least odd representative of the signature, obtained by assigning the largest exponents to the smallest odd primes. Thus the signature value does not exceed its least odd representative excludes every odd integer of that signature. The verifier exhausts all 1211 integer partitions of sizes 1 through 17: every partition through size 16 is excluded, and exactly three size-17 signatures satisfy the signature value exceeds its least odd representative. The least boundary representative is 488462349375 and its exact value is 523830280192. Separate direct recurrences on all 1080 divisors of that integer and all 720 divisors of the source example reproduce the signature-based values.

value.rationale: Odd ample numbers are explicitly identified as rare in the primary source, so total prime-factor multiplicity is a natural structural measure. The result determines the exact first possible total-multiplicity layer, supplies a sharp witness, and classifies the three exponent signatures capable of occurring there. This is a natural complete boundary classification rather than a chosen numerical search cutoff, and it distinguishes structural complexity from the already-known least odd ample integer by numerical size.
